_comment: Every step the Tapstitch web editor needs, as configuration rather than code. Tapstitch has no public API, so product creation goes through their editor; when they redesign it, this file is what gets repaired, not the runner. EVERY null below is unknown and must be filled in during the first live session with the editor open. scripts/tapstitch_publish.py refuses to run while any required value is null and prints exactly which ones are missing.
_first_session_checklist: ANSWERED 15 Sep 2026, YES. The save is PUT /api/designs/customized/templates/<templateId> and it carries piece, src, left, top, width, height, scaleX, scaleY and angle. Every step of product creation is a JSON call. See docs/discovery/2026-09-tapstitch-editor-api.md. The selectors block below is probably dead, but NO CALL HAS BEEN REPLAYED yet, so it is kept until a scripted call is proven to work against one throwaway product.

PARTLY ANSWERED 15 Sep 2026. Tapstitch identifies colours by NUMERIC CODE (colorCode 8079,8088,8084,8085,8081 for the tee), so the API route cannot suffer a swatch-name typo. The check is NOT retired: shopify_fixups.py still matches on names, so colorway_renames_by_type must agree with whatever Tapstitch publishes to Shopify.

ANSWERED 15 Sep 2026, YES. Both files registered at 4386x5516, exactly the tee's real print area, and front and back got identical left/top/width/height/scale with only src differing. Uniform scale, no distortion.
ANSWERED 15 Sep 2026, YES. No re-crop was observed; the print-area-shaped file was accepted as-is.
Do one temple end to end by hand before letting the runner touch the catalogue.

urls._note: Filled from the address bar 15 Sep 2026. new_product was retired the same night: the observed flow never used one, because a design is created by POSTing the blank's SKU to api.create_template. It is kept in _selectors_superseded_by_api for the record.

timing._note: Uploads of 4500x5100 PNGs and the publish-to-Shopify round trip are both slow. The Printify pipeline learned that publishes can far exceed a 240s window and still complete, so the runner confirms against Shopify rather than trusting the editor's own success state.

post_publish._set_product_type_note: LOAD-BEARING. Tapstitch publishes with an EMPTY productType, and every fixup in scripts/shopify_fixups.py is keyed on it, so colour ordering and the featured photo silently do nothing without this. Measured 14 Sep 2026; see docs/discovery/2026-09-tapstitch-store-findings.md.
post_publish._delete_old_listing_note: Evan's decision, 14 Sep 2026: the old Printify listing is deleted at the moment its replacement publishes, so the replacement inherits the same web address. A DRAFT or ARCHIVED product keeps its handle reserved and would push the replacement to a '-1' handle, breaking the Easify dropdown URLs.

api._comment: The editor's own endpoints, observed 15 Sep 2026 and NOT yet replayed. Relative to https://www.tapstitch.com. See docs/discovery/2026-09-tapstitch-editor-api.md for payload shapes and for what is still unverified.
api._method_note: save_design is a PUT. create_template, register_* and create_store_product are POSTs. The image bytes go by PUT straight to the OSS URL that retrieve_upload_data returns.

blanks._unknown: crew (R00368) and hoodie (R00286) were not exercised; they print DTF and their ids and colour codes are unknown.

api._status: PROVEN 15 Sep 2026 for create_template, retrieve_upload_data + OSS PUT, and save_design, each verified by reading the design back. create_store_product is UNRUN: it is the step that reaches a live storefront and needs Evan's decision first.
_traps: x-oss-meta-author is a SIGNED header on the OSS upload. Omit it and the PUT is a bare 403 with a valid, fresh signature. Its value is retrieve-upload-data's `author` field.
Upload lands on the OSS bucket host; a design must reference it on files.tapstitch.com. Same path, different host.
A rejected call still returns HTTP 200. Check the envelope's `code`, not the status line.

A malformed save returns code 10001 'System error, please refresh and try again', which says nothing. It means a required key is missing: virtualConfig, mockupConfig, or per-object clipId / customAreaId / designPart / flipX / flipY / visible.
srcDetails.srcId is NOT required, so the multipart user_cover_img/save call can be skipped entirely.

_selectors_superseded_by_api._note: DEAD as of 15 Sep 2026. These described a click path through the web editor. There is no need to click: every step is a JSON call, proven by replaying them from Python the same evening (a design was created, uploaded to and saved, and Tapstitch rendered four mockups from it). Use tapstitch_api.py. Kept here, not deleted, because nothing has driven the FULL path yet -- the store-product call is still unrun -- so if the API route turns out to have a hole, this is the map back to the fallback.

values._design_size_note: The one number typed into the size field every run. Because the file is the exact shape of the print area, the same value works for every temple on a given garment. Record it per garment if they differ.
